questions.question_text: Which of the following is a relative contraindication to brief time-limited psychotherapeutic approach?

options.text: Having simple and speci�c problems to be addressed
Good ability to form trusting relationships

questions.explanation: Chronic maladaptive patterns tend to be deeply wired and need longer therapies.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following, if present, reduces the suitability of a patient for psychoanalytic psychotherapy?

options.text: Ability to form and sustain relationships

questions.explanation:
Poor frustration tolerance and impulsivity seen in antisocial PD are among the factors indicating poor suitability for psychoanalytic modes of
therapy.

questions.question_text: What predicts a poor response to psychodynamic psychotherapy?

options.text: Good impulse control and good frustration tolerance
Patient can understand things in psychological terms

questions.explanation:
Repeated uncontrolled self-harm can interfere signi�cantly with the psychotherapy. In general, such patients are not suitable for a
psychodynamic approach.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a cognitive technique used in CBT?
questions.explanation:
The overall purpose of Socratic questioning is to challenge accuracy and completeness of thinking in a way that acts to move people towards
their ultimate goal.

questions.question_text: Interpersonal therapy does not focus on one of the following areas.
questions.explanation:
Examples of areas covered are disputes with friends, family or co-workers, grief and loss and role transitions, such as retirement or divorce.
Attachment issues are not dealt in IPT.

questions.question_text: Unconditional positive regard is a feature of
questions.explanation:
Client-centred therapy by Carl Rogers emphasises the importance of therapeutic attributes of genuineness, unconditional positive regard
and accurate empathy.

questions.question_text: Which of the following therapies use 'mindfulness' as a therapeutic strategy?
questions.explanation: Core mindfulness training i.e. learning to monitor internal mental states, is a characteristic feature of DBT.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a self-rating scale?
questions.explanation:
Self-rating scale-Beck depression inventory, hospital anxiety and depression scale and Zung depression rating scale. Observer rating scales-
Hamilton rating scale for depression, Montgomery Asberg depression rating scale, Young Mania Scale and Yale-brown obsessive compulsive
scale.

questions.question_text: Which of the following predicts poor treatment response in chronic fatigue syndrome when treated with CBT/graded exercise?
questions.explanation:
Predictors of poor outcome when treating CFS include (Powell et al, 2004) 1. claiming a disability related bene�t 2. low sense of control 3.
strong focus on physical symptoms 4. being passive with reduced activity and 5. membership of self help group (Note: this does not mean
that self help groups worsen CFS; membership may be an indicator of perceived severity)

questions.question_text: Defence mechanisms are a function of the
questions.explanation:
The �rst systematic account of defence mechanisms was written by Freud's daughter Anna Freud in the book 'Ego and the Mechanisms of
Defence' in 1936.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is not a goal of cognitive therapy?
questions.explanation: The goals of cognitive therapy are to identify negative cognitions, test the validity of those cognitions and revise cognitive assumptions.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a behavioural technique used in CBT?
questions.explanation:
The therapist is very active in CBT and assists the patient to monitor cognitions, identify cognitive errors, understand maladaptive schema
and explore with them strategies to challenge and change these and examine the resultant symptomatic e�ects. The cognitive techniques
include psychoeducation, including reading assignments, identifying automatic thoughts, Socratic questioning, role play, thoughts diary,
thought rehearsal, examining the evidence and working through the options. The behavioural techniques include activity scheduling, graded
assignments, exposure, response prevention, distraction, relaxation training and assertiveness and social skills training.

questions.question_text: Leader assertiveness is one of the therapeutic factors described in
questions.explanation:
The therapeutic factors described by Yalom in Group psychotherapy include altruism, catharsis, corrective recapitulation of the group,
development of socialising techniques, existential awareness, group cohesiveness, instillation of hope, imparting of information,
interpersonal learning, imitative behaviour and universality.

questions.question_text: Which of the following has a healing e�ect in a group setting?
questions.explanation:
Of all the described therapeutic factors (TFs), the mechanism of cohesion is the most central that facilitates the action of other TFs. Cohesion
is the best de�nition of the therapeutic relationship in group (Retrieved from guidelines-for-group-psychotherapy).

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is NOT a curative factor in group therapies?
questions.explanation:
Yalom cited 11 'curative' factors responsible for change in groups. The curative factors include instillation of hope, universality, imparting
information (feedback), altruism, corrective recapitulation, socialisation techniques, imitative behaviour, interpersonal learning, group
cohesiveness, catharsis and existential factors. Of these, cohesiveness, and learning from feedback are valued positively though other
factors may also be important.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a component of the Dialectic Behavioural Therapy proposed by Linehan?
questions.explanation: The core skill areas in DBT include mindfulness, distress tolerance, emotion regulation, and interpersonal e�ectiveness.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is least likely to be correct concerning Camberwell Family Interview?

options.text: Ratings based on interviewing parents singly had the most predictive value.
It is used to measure EE levels

questions.explanation:
CFI is a long interview process where individual members of a family are interviewed (including the patient). If one relative is classi�ed as
high EE relative, the family is termed a high EE family. It was found that ratings based on interviewing parents individually had the most
predictive value.

questions.question_text: Rolling with resistance is a technique used as a major component in which of the following psychotherapies?
questions.explanation:
Resistance is a predictive of poor treatment outcomes and lack of involvement in the therapeutic process. Rolling with resistance is a
technique used in motivational interviewing.

questions.question_text: Which one among the following is not considered to be a Neo-Freudian?
questions.explanation:
Neo-Freudians are thinkers who agree with the basis of Freud's psychoanalytic theory, but change or adapt it to incorporate their own
beliefs, ideas and theories. Piaget is not considered as a Freudian theorist.

questions.question_text:
A depressed schoolteacher thinks 'one student in the class is sleeping, so the entire class is bored of my lecture'. The cognitive distortion in
this scenario is
questions.explanation: This is one of the many cognitive distortions described by Beck.

questions.question_text: Interpersonal Psychotherapy is associated with the following except

options.text: Runs from 12 to 16 hourly sessions, usually occurring weekly

questions.explanation: Cognitive analytical therapy focuses on snags and dilemmas. IPT focuses on grief and role transitions.

questions.question_text: which one among the following is not correctly paired?

options.text: Malan and Davanloo - Brief dynamic therapy

questions.explanation:
Palazolli and colleagues from Milan are associated with systemic family therapy - not structural therapy. Strategic family therapy is
associated with Haley. Haley called the therapy Strategic because "it is a therapy where the therapist initiates what happens during therapy,
designs a speci�c approach for each person's presenting problem, and takes responsibility for directly in�uencing people" (Retrieved from

questions.question_text: Which of the following behavioural treatment is useful in trichotillomania?
questions.explanation:
Habit reversal training (HRT) is a behavioral treatment package useful in tics and other OCD spectrum disorders such as trichotillomania, nail
biting, thumb sucking, and skin picking etc.

questions.question_text: Psychodynamic therapy can be used for a wide variety of disorders. But it is contraindicated for which of the following?
questions.explanation:
Psychodynamic psychotherapy is generally avoided in acute psychosis, very high risk of recurrent DSH and conditions where there is acute
suicidal risk, delirium, dementia, very severe depressive illness and in drug and alcohol misuse. Indicators that a patient is likely to respond
to psychotherapy include a good response to a trial interpretation, a tendency for self-re�ection, presence of realistic expectations, a
reasonable degree of personality integration and a motivation for change.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following techniques is considered to be anti-therapeutic in group therapy?
questions.explanation:
Scape goating, idealization of the therapist and coupling are considered to be anti-therapeutic in group therapy. Scapegoating is an
explanation of discrimination based on the idea of frustration-aggression.The work of Bion, Ezriel and Foulkes were crucial in the
development of group therapy.

questions.question_text: The basis of object relations theory is that the primary motivational drive of an individual is to seek
questions.explanation:
Object relations theory describes with how a growing baby develops relationships with others. Grati�cation is thought to be obtained
through relationships as well as through satisfaction of desires.

questions.question_text:
A 25-year-old bride is getting ready for her wedding. She thinks that if she is late for her wedding, then her bridegroom will refuse to marry
her, and she will be left on her own forever. Choose one cognitive distortion that is most likely
questions.explanation:
Catastrophisation is a cognitive distortion that refers to the tendency of always predicting the worst case scenario to happen. E.g. A woman
with panic attacks can sense mild palpitation after some house work, and thinks she is going to have a massive heart attack and immediate
death.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is not included in Bion's basic assumptions?
questions.explanation:
According to Bion, whenever a group gets derailed from its task, it deteriorates into one of the three basic states: dependency, pairing, or
�ght-�ight. A 4th basic assumption was introduced by Hopper called massi�cation/aggregation where a rigid fusion of identities leads to loss
of individuality, or extensive withdrawal leads to loss of mutual dependence.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following often seen in the process of supportive psychotherapy?

options.text: Patient seeking exploration of cause of symptoms

questions.explanation:
Supportive therapy aims to o�er practical and emotional support, provides an opportunity for ventilation of emotions and guided problem
solving discussions. The primary aim of supportive psychotherapy is to support reality testing, provide ego support and attempt to
reestablish usual level of functioning. It is usually employed in otherwise healthy patients with overwhelming ongoing crises and those with
ego de�cits.

questions.question_text: What predicts a good response to dynamic psychotherapy?

options.text: Positive perception of the therapist throughout treatment
Motivation developed after sustained e�ort from therapist
Patient can understand issues in psychological terms

correct_answer.text: Patient can understand issues in psychological terms

questions.explanation:
A curiosity to understand and reformulate problems in terms of one's life experiences or psychological structure is an important predictor of
response to psychotherapy.

questions.question_text: Genetic counselling is classi�ed under which type of counselling?
questions.explanation:
Counselling may be thought of as a method of relieving distress undertaken by means of a dialogue between two people. The aim is to help
the client or patient �nd their own solutions to problems, while being supported to do so and being guided by appropriate advice. The
di�erent types include psycho education, crisis management, problem-based counselling directed towards a speci�c primary problem, e.g.
drug misuse and risk counselling used to guide an informed decision (e.g. pre-natal interventions, genetic counselling). The latter is
di�erentiated from other forms of counselling by the fact that the counsellor is clearly the expert and has access to specialist information.

questions.question_text: Idealization and denigration are products of which of the following Kleinian processes?
questions.explanation:
Splitting refers to splitting of self into good and bad. Idealization and devaluation (denigration) are the results of splitting and are central in
the Kleinian school of thought.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following group therapies has a high level of leader input?

options.text: Structured groups for drug or alcohol use

correct_answer.text: Structured groups for drug or alcohol use

questions.explanation:
Group therapies can be classi�ed according to the objectives of the group and how the group is led or managed (leadership). Highly speci�c
target oriented groups include structured groups for drug use or alcohol use, activity groups like occupational therapy, groups etc. These
groups have high level of leader input. Psychodrama, music therapy, systems centred groups are some less speci�c therapies but are highly
directed by the leader or therapist. Problem solving therapy and psycho educational groups are highly speci�c but have low level of
therapist activity. Support groups, art therapy, interpersonal therapy and groups like Tavistock model analytic groups have low level of
leader activity and have low speci�city with respect to treatment goals

questions.question_text: The de�nite termination date is set at beginning of treatment in which of the following therapies?
questions.explanation:
Brief psychodynamic psychotherapy is a time-limited treatment that is based on psychoanalysis and psychodynamic theory. Brief
psychodynamic therapy is an intervention where the concepts of symptom development and methods of therapy are based on those of
psychoanalysis and are more focused on the here and now- the patient's current experience of the world, and techniques are employed to
accelerate the process of therapy but where the time scale and number of sessions are reduced.

questions.question_text: Which of the following therapies uses techniques such as circular questioning and hypothesising?
questions.explanation:
The Milan systemic approach (Selvini Palazzoli et al, 1978) has been modi�ed over the years, from its original paradoxical prescriptions to a
great emphasis on a particular style of interviewing – circular and re�exive questioning (Selvini Palazzoli et al, 1980). This technique focuses
on questioning the various family members' beliefs and perceptions regarding relationships. Asking each to comment and re�ect on the
answers given by the various family members creates feedback that changes the fabric of family interactions (Retrieved from

questions.question_text: Thought stopping is a behavioural technique used in
questions.explanation:
Additional behaviour and cognitive-behavioral techniques which may have some e�ectiveness for people who su�er from obsessive
compulsive disorder include saturation and thought-stopping. Saturation is a process where the patient is directed to think repeatedly of the
most intrusive obsessional thought. After an extended period of concentration on this one thought (e.g., 10-15 minutes at a time) over a
number of days (3-5 days), the obsession can lose some of its strength. Thought-stopping is a technique where the patient learns how to halt
obsessive thoughts through identi�cation of the obsessional thoughts, and then averting them by carrying out a strong, incompatible
response.

questions.question_text: An e�ective technique for treating hypochondriasis is
questions.explanation:
In the treatment of hypochondriasis, it is important to break the cycle of reassurance and repeat presentation. Behavioural experiments
focused on response prevention and exposure to illness cues is the most e�ective strategy in the management. This could be done as a part
of CBT (The role of CBT is to identify and challenge misinterpretations, substitution of realistic interpretation, graded exposure to illness
related situations and modi�cation of core beliefs).

questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes the stance that is held by the therapist while administering Interpersonal Psychotherapy?
questions.explanation:
In IPT, the therapist is an explicit ally and advocate of the patient. The therapist is nonjudgmental, expresses warmth and positive regard for
the patient and congratulates the patient as progress in the problem areas is made. The therapist works with the patient and for the patient
and believes that the patient's problems can be solved. This does not imply that the therapist accepts all aspects of the patient, as that
would preclude any stimulus for change. The therapist always tries to have the patient �nd the solution for the problems discussed in the
session. However, the therapist is not afraid to make suggestions or provide direct advice when they seem useful.

questions.question_text: Which one among the following is not one of the therapeutic techniques used in Interpersonal therapy?
questions.explanation:
The therapeutic techniques in IPT are speci�c to the problem under review and includes relationship problem-solving, facilitation of grief,
catharsis and role-play. The role disputes can be resolved by renegotiation, acceptation of impasse or dissolution. Free association is a
Freudian concept not relevant for IPT.

questions.question_text: Systematic desensitization involves all of the following steps except
questions.explanation:
Systematic Desensitisation (Wolpe) is ased on the behavioral principle of counter conditioning (i.e. gradual approach of feared situation in a
psychophysiological state that inhibits anxiety leads to reduction of anxiety response.) Systematic desensitization consists of three steps:
relaxation training, hierarchy construction, and desensitization of the stimulus. The patient is exposed to a graded hierarchy of anxiety-
provoking situations in step wise fashion.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is considered as a mature defence mechanism?
questions.explanation:
Primitive/immature defenses include splitting, projection, projective identi�cation, idealization, denigration, introjection, passive aggression
and turning against the self. Neurotic defences include repression, regression, denial, displacement, dissociation, isolation, reaction
formation, intellectualisation, rationalization, externalisation and identi�cation with the aggressor. Humour, anticipation, sublimation,
altruism and suppression (SASHA) are all mature defence mechanisms.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a technique used in motivational interviewing?
questions.explanation:
When using motivational interviewing, one does not �ght client resistance, but instead 'rolls with it.' Resistance can take several forms, such
negating, blaming, etc.

questions.question_text: Which one among the following is NOT a part of the Beck's theory of depression?
questions.explanation:
Beck's cognitive model of depression includes two levels of cognitive errors that include automatic thoughts and core schemas. The
cognitive errors include selective abstraction, arbitrary inference, minimisation, magni�cation, all or nothing thinking, personalisation,
catastrophic thinking and overgeneralization. Turning against self is a psychodynamic concept of depression.

questions.question_text: Who described the unconscious as composed of both the collective unconscious and personal unconscious?
questions.explanation:
Carl Gustav Jung described a holisitc theory of psyche that could be applied across varied cultures. According to him, the unconscious mind
includes the collective and personal unconscious. He postulated that the personal unconscious is unique to each but the collective
unconscious is universal, common to mankind, contains the archetypes that include anima, animus, shadow or self and Hero.

questions.question_text:
Nursing sta� at a learning disability care home are concerned about the self-injurious behaviour of a 40-year-old man. A psychologist is
called for conducting a functional behavioral analysis. On which of the following information would she concentrate?

options.text: The immediate consequences of the patient's self injury at the care home setting
Past history of parental child abuse

correct_answer.text: The immediate consequences of the patient's self injury at the care home setting

questions.explanation: In behavioural analysis, one looks at antecedent, behaviour and its consequences.

questions.question_text: Strategic family therapy is o�ered to a dysfunctional family. What technique is mainly used in this therapy?
questions.explanation:
Task setting (homework tasks) are an essential component of strategic family therapy. The use of tasks in family therapy is consistent with
the model's emphasis on having family members 'do' rather than simply 'talk about'. The tasks are relatively easier in the early part of
treatment to foster a sense of success. Tasks tend to be more complex later in the treatment. In all instances, the therapists create
opportunities for family members to practice and demonstrate competence in the task, prior to assigning homework.

questions.question_text:
The closeness between two family members may exclude a third member. Study of these triangular patterns of relationships in family takes
place in
questions.explanation:
Bowen's model (family systems approach) emphasizes one's ability to retain individual self in the face of familial tension. The degree of
enmeshment is analysed here. An emotional triangle is a three-party system where closeness of two members (in either positive or negative
sense) tends to exclude a third. This hot triangle leads to symptom formation. Here therapist maintains minimal emotional contact with
family members.

questions.question_text: Which school of family therapy are associated with the use of an ONE-way mirror?
questions.explanation:
The Milan systemic approach (Palazolli) gives great emphasis on circular and re�exive questioning. In a circular fashion, each family member
is asked to comment and re�ect on each others response. The Milan systemic school of family therapy is associated with the use of an ONE-
way mirror.

questions.question_text:
You are called to see a newly admitted patient with personality disorder in the ward; you notice that the nursing sta� are angry and feel
unwanted by the patient. What is the most likely psychological explanation?
questions.explanation:
Projective identi�cation (not just projection) has taken place here. The patient has projected her own 'hatred' on the therapists (nurses), and
they are identifying themselves with the projected material and are acting in a way showing the hatred (identi�cation). This is a mechanism
explaining counter-transference.

questions.question_text: The 'repressive barrier' to censor unacceptable wishes and desires is maintained by
questions.explanation:
The preconscious interfaces with both unconscious and conscious - contents of unconscious become conscious by 'squeezing' through the
preconscious. It maintains the 'repressive barrier' to censor unacceptable wishes and desires (not the repressed contents).

questions.question_text: Which type of group psychotherapy is used for the treatment of phobias?
questions.explanation: Behavioural groups can be organised to provide group therapy in a resource e�cient manner for phobias.

questions.question_text: The focus of attention is childhood experience and exploration of the unconscious mind in which of the following forms of therapy?
questions.explanation:
Psychodynamic therapy upholds psychic determinism i.e. unconscious events play a causal role in later experiences. It emphasizes
developmental psychopathology as the source of adult life di�culties.

questions.question_text: The �rst step in management of someone presenting with fear of spiders is

options.text: Detailed history for a functional assessment

correct_answer.text: Detailed history for a functional assessment

questions.explanation: Before applying any behavioural treatment approach, a detailed history is required.

questions.question_text: Which type of family therapy encourages clear and open boundaries between the parents and the children?
questions.explanation:
There are several types of family therapy based on the psychotherapeutic method applied. Structural family therapy developed by Minuchin
emphasises that the structure of the family is maintained by unspoken rules and when the roles are broken the structure is weakened
leading to problems in the family. Minuchin originally worked with families of psychosomatic and eating disordered patients. The Milan
systemic school of family therapy is associated with the use of a ONE-way mirror. It is also associated with the concepts of paradoxes
(vicious circle in which the family is trapped), circular questioning, neutrality and hypothesising. The strategic family therapy emphasises
more active interventions and speci�c solutions for clearly de�ned family problem.

questions.question_text:
During on of your psychotherapy sessions, a patient reveals that he has been abusing his children, but suddenly he changes the topic. What
should you do?

options.text: Keep your boundaries and end the session as planned.
Terminate the interview immediately and inform the social services.
Tell him you will inform the concerned authority
Clarify what he means by abuse
Ignore and continue with the �ow the patients talk

correct_answer.text: Clarify what he means by abuse

questions.explanation: People might hold varying meanings for commonly used expressions. It is necessary to seek clari�cation before proceeding further.

questions.question_text: Positive prognostic indicators for psychotherapy include all of the following except

options.text: good response to a trial interpretation

questions.explanation:
In general psychotic disorders have been traditionally considered to involve ego disintegration and hence not suitable for therapeutic
working through.

questions.question_text: In psychotherapy, the term psychological mindedness refers to which of the following?

options.text: Ability to form a therapeutic alliance
The ability to understand problems in physical terms
The ability to understand problems in psychological terms

correct_answer.text: The ability to understand problems in psychological terms

questions.explanation:
The term psychological mindedness refers to an ability to understand problems in psychological terms. Ego strength is a term coined by
Freud, and it includes the ability to sustain feelings and fantasies without impulsively acting upon them.

questions.question_text: The cognitive outcome you would hope to achieve when treating someone with hypochondriasis is

options.text: The complete absence of thoughts of illness.
Ability to avoid medical help seeking when symptoms are troublesome
Less distress at thoughts of illness

correct_answer.text: Less distress at thoughts of illness

questions.explanation:
CBT for hypochondriasis aims to generate a noncatastrophic alternative psychological explanation for a patient's problems. An RCT
concluded that a six-session CBT intervention modestly but signi�cantly improved a range of hypochondriacal symptoms, beliefs, and
attitudes at six and 12 months. These results may not be generalisable as only 30 percent of eligible patients agreed for CBT trial. It is
unclear which components of CBT really work in hypochondriasis. Hypochondriasis often is refractory to treatment and improvement
involved better coping methods rather than cure. Role functioning may improve as a functional outcome. Reduced distress associated with
beliefs rather than eradication of beliefs is the primary outcome expected (Barsky et al 2004).

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is not a component of CBT for delusions in psychosis?

options.text: Decreasing the impact of positive symptoms
Providing alternate explanations to unusual experiences

questions.explanation:
Though CBT is gaining popularity in treating psychotic symptoms, often, clinicians are unsure about the symptoms targeted in CBT.
According to Birchwood, the target is the emotional dysfunction that accompanies psychotic experience and not the psychotic symptoms
per se. Turkington described the following elements in CBT for psychosis: Therapeutic alliance, Improving medication adherence, Providing
alternate explanations to unusual experiences e.g. normalisation, Decreasing the impact of positive symptoms e.g. addressing the
omnipotence of voices and Graded reality testing using peripheral questioning and inference chaining.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the best description of Bion's principle of containing?

options.text: Therapist manages to exclude distortion of one patient's story from another patient's experiences.
Therapist maintains objectivity and focuses on facts
Therapist doesn't let his feelings out and restrains himself.
Therapist advises the patient to contain the feelings without letting them out.
Patient has to explore the feelings within and relate them to the surroundings.

correct_answer.text: Therapist maintains objectivity and focuses on facts

questions.explanation:
The cognitive capacity of the therapist to maintain objectivity and focus on selected facts during a discourse is called 'containing' (Bion). The
a�ective disposition of the therapist, which helps in restraining oneself from retaliating to negative transferences, is called 'holding.'

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a correct description of transference?

options.text: Good eye contact throughout therapy session
Patient's response to the therapist based on previous relationships

correct_answer.text: Patient's response to the therapist based on previous relationships

questions.explanation:
Transference is an unconscious process that involves transferring a part of one's past relationship in an at least partly inappropriate fashion
to the present life situation.

questions.question_text:
A psychotherapist feels that she is talking a lot to a patient and o�ering a lot of advice during therapy. This is because something in the
patient's life is causing anxiety in her. This phenomenon is known as
questions.explanation:
Transference is the phenomenon whereby we unconsciously transfer feelings and attitudes from a person or situation in the past on to a
person or situation in the present (Retrieved from  Countertransference is the
response that is elicited in the recipient (therapist) by the other's (patient's) unconscious transference communications.

questions.question_text: All of the following are described by Yalom as group curative factors, except
questions.explanation:
Yalom cited 11 'curative' factors responsible for the change in groups. The curative factors include the instillation of hope, universality,
imparting information (feedback), altruism, corrective recapitulation, socialisation techniques, imitative behaviour, interpersonal learning,
group cohesiveness, catharsis and existential factors. Of these, cohesiveness, and learning from feedback are valued positively though other
factors may also be important.

questions.question_text: Which theory best suits the explanation for someone with an emotionally unstable personality disorder?
questions.explanation:
Klein's paranoid-schizoid position best explains the splitting, idealisation, denigration and persecutory anxiety seen in borderline personality
disorder.

questions.question_text: Your colleague asks you what has been shown to predict a good response to psychotherapy for depression. Your response will be

options.text: Lack of prior exposure to therapy
The therapist's contribution to therapeutic alliance
The patient's perception of the working alliance with the therapist.

correct_answer.text: The patient's perception of the working alliance with the therapist.

questions.explanation:
The relationship between therapeutic alliance and treatment outcome was examined for depressed outpatients who received interpersonal
psychotherapy, cognitive-behavior therapy, imipramine with clinical management, or placebo with clinical management in NIMH
collaborative trial for depression treatment (Krupnick et al, 2006). Therapeutic alliance was found to have a signi�cant e�ect on clinical
outcome for both psychotherapies and for active and placebo pharmacotherapy. Ratings of patient contribution to the alliance were
signi�cantly related to treatment outcome; ratings of therapist contribution to the alliance and outcome were not signi�cantly linked. These
results indicate that the therapeutic alliance is a common factor with signi�cant in�uence on outcome ( The role of the therapeutic alliance
in psychotherapy and ... (n.d.). Retrieved from  Positive perception of therapist throughout
treatment (idealization) is not necessary and may even be counterproductive in some cases.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a crucial step in the psychological treatment of phobias?
questions.explanation:
The important step and powerful step in the treatment of speci�c phobia is to begin confronting feared situations in real life. The
desensitization process begins with making a hierarchy, a graded list of situations that cause anxiety. Systematic desensitization consists of
three steps: relaxation training, hierarchy construction, and desensitization of the stimulus. Patient is exposed to a graded hierarchy of
anxiety-provoking situations in stepwise fashion

questions.question_text: The approach of mentalisation is best utilised in which of the following therapies?
questions.explanation:
MBT focuses on understanding your mental state, such as emotions, feelings, and thoughts and that of others so you can manage your
emotions and improve your relationships. Mentalization-Based Therapy (MBT) provides a way to increase your capacity to make personal
attachments and therefore reduce the emotional intensity you experience. Initial research has proved that mentalization is e�ective for BPD
treatment as compared to the usual treatments in the �eld. It shows signi�cant reduction in suicide attempts and suicidal ideation,
hospitalization due to suicidal or feelings of/intent to self-harm, and trips to the emergency room.

questions.question_text: Which of the following types of psychotherapy is suitable in a child with learning di�culties and behavioural dyscontrol?
questions.explanation:
Behavioural therapy is suitable in a child with learning di�culties and behavioural dyscontrol. It involves modi�cation of behaviour using
operant conditioning (rewarding good behaviour, removal of aversive stimuli, neutral response to attention seeking behaviour), secondary
reinforcers, modelling and positive programming.

questions.question_text:
Which of the following modes of therapies has the least empirical evidence in terms of e�cacy for borderline personality disorder and not
recommended by NICE?
questions.explanation:
Acceptance and Commitment Therapy or ACT has the least empirical evidence in terms of e�cacy for borderline personality disorder. It is an
empirically-based psychological intervention that uses acceptance and mindfulness strategies mixed in di�erent ways with commitment and
behavior-change strategies, to increase psychological �exibility. ACT has shown preliminary research evidence of e�ectiveness in
randomized trials for a variety of problems including chronic pain, addictions, smoking cessation, depression, anxiety, workplace stress,
diabetes management, weight management etc
